output.brief: The slowdown comes from one change, not from Corvane or the new hires. Credit Policy v14 took effect on 1 May. It requires a full inspection appraisal for property collateral above $150k, where the old threshold was $500k. Full appraisals take about 8.6 days from the valuation firm. Desktop valuations take about 1.2 days. Appraisals for this band rose from about 30 to about 80 a month. For property-secured loans the valuation stage went from 1.6 days in March to 8.4 in August. Every other stage is flat, including document collection at the five branches with new hires. Unsecured loans are back to about 5.9 days, and consumer loans on Corvane are unchanged. The valuation firm's turnaround hasn't changed. The policy's impact on processing times was never assessed. The rise in withdrawals fits the slowdown, but I haven't shown it causes withdrawals. Corvane's 30-day auto-close rule also counts as withdrawals some files that the old system left open. I'm fairly confident in this diagnosis (about 85%). Next, take the measured delay to the credit risk committee alongside the audit rationale, and ask whether to amend the $150k threshold or speed up the appraisal process. Don't withhold the Corvane payment or put the new hires on improvement plans. Add a by-stage breakdown to the dashboard. Check the withdrawal closure codes before offering any customer incentive.
